Dylan's live debut with the Grateful Dead, on the first of three songs he joined during set one after his own opening set with Tom Petty. Dead.net attendee: 'Dylan joining them for Little Red Rooster, Don't Think Twice and Baby Blue,' checked against handwritten notes; setlist.fm.

Dylan on lead vocals, the only time the Grateful Dead ever played this song, during his first sit-in at the Rubber Bowl. Setlist.fm; dead.net July 2 1986 show page attendee comment naming the same three-song set.

Dylan and Garcia shared vocals to close his three-song sit-in. The same night's later Desolation Row is marked 'no Jerry' by an attendee and is not counted as a Dylan song here. Setlist.fm; dead.net show page comments.

Five days after Akron, Dylan sat in again at RFK Stadium. His guitar was not working at the start of the song and he finished it on a borrowed Bob Weir guitar. Setlist.fm; dead.net July 7 1986 show page attendee comment.
The two Bobs traded verses on this Dylan original, the second of two songs he sat in on at RFK Stadium. Setlist.fm; dead.net show page comment: 'the Desolation Row with the two Bobs trading lyrics.'

Dylan walked out to open the second set on this song, the start of a run some attendees believe he helped choose that night. JamBase, 'Bob Dylan, Spencer Davis & Kitaro Join Grateful Dead In 1989'; Grateful Dead of the Day, February 12 1989.

A bust-out with Dylan onstage, the song's first performance since 1981. Grateful Dead of the Day: 'some people who were there claim that Dylan was calling the setlist,' which would explain the choice. JamBase confirms the song and the gap.

Part of the pre-Drums stretch of the second set that JamBase and Grateful Dead of the Day both credit to Dylan, alongside Iko Iko, Monkey and the Engineer, Dire Wolf, Cassidy and Stuck Inside of Mobile.
One of six second-set songs in a row with Dylan onstage before Drums. JamBase, 'Bob Dylan, Spencer Davis & Kitaro Join Grateful Dead In 1989'; Grateful Dead of the Day, February 12 1989.

Dylan stayed on through this song's jam; a dead.net attendee wrote he 'clearly looked baffled during the jam in Cassidy,' finding structured songs easier than open jamming. Dead.net show page comment; JamBase.

The night's centerpiece: Weir sang Dylan's own song and stalled mid-verse, and Dylan finished the line himself. One attendee: 'Bobby kept trying to get Dylan to sing... he didn't want to' until Weir 'pretended to forget the lyrics.' JamBase; dead.net show page.

Dylan came back out for the two-song encore after sitting out Drums, Space, The Other One, Stella Blue and Foolish Heart. Dead.net: he 'returned for both encore songs.' JamBase, 'Bob Dylan, Spencer Davis & Kitaro Join Grateful Dead In 1989.'

Dylan's last song of the night. JamBase says he took the band through it; a dead.net commenter recalls Weir singing lead while Dylan 'let Bobby sing Heaven's Door.' Either way he stayed onstage to close the show.

The Grateful Dead's only performance of this song, and their first Dylan collaboration since the 1989 Forum sit-in. His microphone failed and Weir stopped playing mid-song to adjust the stand. JamBase, 'Bob Dylan Performs With Grateful Dead At Madison Square Garden On This Date In 1994'; dead.net show page comments.

Phil Lesh invited Marsalis backstage and the band auditioned him on Bird Song before asking him to stay for the whole second set. JamBase, 'Watch Branford Marsalis Make Grateful Dead Debut At Nassau Coliseum.'
Marsalis opened the second set he'd just been asked to stay for with Eyes of the World, later the opening track of the official release Wake Up to Find Out. Wikipedia, 'Wake Up to Find Out.'
Marsalis continued through Estimated Prophet, the second set's second song. JamBase, 'Watch Branford Marsalis Make Grateful Dead Debut At Nassau Coliseum.'
Marsalis had never played Dark Star and asked the band 'What is it?' before the first of two takes that night. JamBase, 'Watch Branford Marsalis Make Grateful Dead Debut At Nassau Coliseum.'

This second Dark Star, after Drums and Space, drew fans who later called Marsalis's private number to thank him for reviving a song the Dead hadn't played in six months. JamBase, 'Watch Branford Marsalis Make Grateful Dead Debut At Nassau Coliseum.'
Marsalis stayed on for The Wheel as the second set continued. JamBase, 'Watch Branford Marsalis Make Grateful Dead Debut At Nassau Coliseum.'

Marsalis closed the second set with Turn On Your Lovelight. JamBase, 'Watch Branford Marsalis Make Grateful Dead Debut At Nassau Coliseum.'
Marsalis returned for the Knockin' On Heaven's Door encore, capping the night later released as Wake Up to Find Out. Wikipedia, 'Wake Up to Find Out.'
